summary.headline: MTAR posted record Q4 FY26 sales of INR306 crore and FY26 revenue of INR876 crore (+30% YoY); FY27 guided to 80%+ growth and ~24% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached a record INR306 crore versus INR183 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR61.8 crore and PAT of about INR44.3 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR876 crore (up about 30%), EBITDA INR171 crore at 19.5% margin (against guidance of around 21% plus or minus 1%), and PAT INR94 crore. Gross margin fell to 47.7% from 49.4%, which management attributed to input cost and freight pressure from geopolitical events and headcount added for expansion. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 80%+ (plus or minus 5%) with EBITDA margin of around 24%, and closing order book guidance of about INR5,000 crore by end-FY27. FY26 closed at INR2,580 crore order book, below the INR2,800 crore earlier guidance, which management attributed to nuclear and defence orders (about INR250 crore) slipping into the current quarter.

segments.name: Clean energy
segments.commentary: Expected to be about 70% of FY27 revenue; initial capacity phase already commissioned and further multifold capacity being built with capex of INR250-300 crore over two years. A new AI data-centre infrastructure customer has given first-article orders of INR35 crore, with potential of INR400-500 crore over the next couple of years.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order book of INR650 crore-plus to be executed over the next 3-3.5 years, the strongest in its history. Refurbishment orders are pending and Mahi Banswara (ASHVINI) new-reactor tenders are expected this year; management says Calandria and end shield qualification is complete.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Orders above INR360 crore; volume production started with some customers. IAI first articles due by September with volume production from October. An LCA Mk1A actuator order of INR130-150 crore is expected, and an AMCA structural assembly first order of INR4 crore has been won.

segments.name: Oil and gas
segments.commentary: Whipstock assembly first articles completed; potential of USD 35-40 million over time. Dedicated plant commissioning by September 2026, with potential INR450-500 crore revenue from that plant over 3-4 years.

segments.name: Product division
segments.commentary: Expected to cross INR200 crore revenue in FY27; qualified for ball screw supply to MNC customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth raised to 80%+ (plus or minus 5%) from earlier guidance of 50%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at around 24%, with margin improvement quarter-on-quarter; management cites about 5% operating leverage on a fixed cost base of about 28%.
Closing FY27 order book estimated at about INR5,000 crore versus INR2,580 crore at end-FY26.
Management expects a strong first half and a stronger second half in FY27, reversing FY26's weak first half.
Working capital days targeted to remain at a similar level by end-FY27; debt-to-equity targeted around 0.5 over the next two years.
Other income for FY27 expected to be supported by a forecast of a weaker rupee, per bankers' forecast.
capex_capacity: Clean energy capex of INR250-300 crore over FY27-FY28 to build multifold capacity for a key customer; management declined to disclose capacity numbers under NDA.
Initial clean-energy expansion phase commissioned; additional capacity to come online by end-FY26 and into FY27.
Oil and gas plant to be commissioned by September 2026 and fully operational thereafter.
Internal estimate of capex needed to reach INR5,000 crore revenue is INR500-700 crore, with incremental capex planned year-on-year.
Greenfield infrastructure being built with phased equipment additions; company is planning automation to reduce manpower dependency.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing is not being renegotiated; gross margin dip of about 190 bps sequentially attributed to input costs and freight, not customer price cuts.
Working capital improvement came from better credit terms negotiated with multiple customers, not one-off advances, per management.
Fluence has been dropped from the customer list; management says prototypes are done and the door is open pending duty clarity on battery exports.
Refurbishment bids are in process for 5 reactors; management expects further refurbishment opportunities as reactors are taken up.
AMCA: tenders floated for structural assemblies with 8 qualified vendors; the earlier Adani collaboration has had no further update.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue split across clean energy, nuclear and defence?
qa_highlights.answer: Clean energy is expected to be about 70% of FY27 revenue; other verticals are growing in absolute terms but more slowly.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed for the clean-energy capacity expansion and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Rough capex of INR250-300 crore, spread over two years (FY27 and FY28), for multiple capacities for one customer.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 growth be back-ended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first half will be very good and the second half much better, reversing FY26's weak first half.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to INR5,000 crore revenue and FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to a date; said there is a clear roadmap to be where it wants to be by FY30 and internal capex estimate of INR500-700 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the working-capital improvement sustainable and are customer advances one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is negotiated payment terms across multiple customers, a continuous process, not one-off advances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear order inflow and revenue visibility in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not quantify FY27 nuclear inflow or timing; said the INR650 crore-plus book executes over 3-3.5 years, with scaling from Q2.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from input and freight costs amid geopolitical uncertainty; 24% EBITDA margin guidance depends on operating leverage.
Timing of nuclear refurbishment and Mahi Banswara tenders; about INR250 crore of orders slipped from FY26 into Q1 FY27.
Ability to convert the INR5,000 crore order book target; FY27 order inflow of about INR40 billion is implied and not yet visible.
Rising debt (about INR370 crore) to fund capacity expansion; management says debt is the current route, with equity raise as an alternative.
Dependence on one large clean-energy customer; competitive vendor additions and the Fluence project remain open questions.
Reliance on forex gains in other income (about INR25 crore) that may not recur.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on growth, capacity and margin targets, with repeated assurances on execution. Evasive on quantification of capex by capacity, nuclear order timing, and the FY30 INR5,000 crore revenue path, where management declined to commit.
